answer1: No, according to Section 8(7)(a) of the Act, a Data Fiduciary like a bank is not required to erase personal data immediately upon the withdrawal of consent by the Data Principal, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law for the time being in force. In the case of closing a savings account, the bank is required to retain the personal data for a period of ten years beyond the closure of the account due to legal necessity.
